title: Architect, tech lead and senior engineer: the boundaries of the role

videos.script: Three people at Carreto write code, review designs and take technical decisions. {{three}} Paula is a senior engineer on Platform, Bruno leads the Payments team, and Renata is the architect. In a busy week, a visitor could not tell their jobs apart. {{axes}} The difference is not seniority. It is scope and horizon: how much of the system a decision touches, and how long it has to hold. Paula's decisions live inside one team for a sprint. Renata's cross seven teams and last for years. {{larson}} Will Larson found the same shapes among staff engineers, and gave them names. {{overlap}} Then the overlaps. In a company of six engineers, one person is all three roles, and that works. At fifty, two people can each believe a decision is theirs. A table of decision rights settles that before the argument starts. {{edges}} The lesson ends where the architect's job ends. Renata manages nobody. She does not own the roadmap. She does not approve every pull request. And no release is ever waiting on her.
